entities.summary: Janata Dal (United) (JD(U), lit. 'People's Party (United)'), is a social democratic and secular Indian political party, rooted mainly in eastern and north-eastern India, whose stated goals are promoting social justice and lifting up marginalised people. JD(U) is recognised as a state party in the states of Bihar, where it heads the government and it is a part of the coalition government in Manipur and Arunachal Pradesh. JD(U), as part of the Bharatiya Janata Party-led National Democratic Alliance, won 12 seats in the 2024 Indian general election, making it the seventh largest party in the Lok Sabha.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Janata Dal (United) has had a significant impact on Indian politics since its founding in 1999, with notable wins in Bihar and Manipur. The party's influence on India's coalition governments and its role in shaping the country's social democratic agenda make it a regional player.
